judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Footer link to the Google Play store page (play.google.com, com.lakeland.android). Its only content is the store badge, and it has aria-label="Download our App". The neighbouring link to the Apple App Store has the same name. The context is the same for both (heading "Download our App", text "For your latest myLakeland vouchers") and does not name the store. Visually the badges say App Store and Google Play, so sighted users can tell the two apart, but a screen-reader user hears two identical "Download our App" links and cannot tell which platform each serves. Following ACT rule fd3a94 (identical names and same context must lead to equivalent resources unless the page itself shows no difference), the two store pages are not equivalent for a given user, and the visual design shows they differ. I checked whether the purpose of downloading the app is the same either way and decided it is not enough: the platform is the part of the purpose that differs. Live page unchanged. Real 2.4.4 failure.

judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: The Google Play badge image inside the footer app link, with alt="Download our App". The crop shows "GET IT ON Google Play". The finding says the alt describes something the image does not show. That is not quite right: "Download our App" matches the badge's call to action and the link's function, which the functional-image guidance asks an alt to give. The real weakness is an omission. The alt leaves out the store name that the image of text shows, and the other badge has the same alt, so the platform information is lost (under G94, the alt does not present the same information). Some auditors would fail 1.1.1 for that. Others would accept the functional alt and file the problem under 2.4.4 (as the link findings do). Auditors could reasonably disagree on whether this fails 1.1.1, and the stated reason does not fit, so I label it uncertain.

judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: This is the Algolia autocomplete wrapper (div role=combobox) in the header search form, with aria-labelledby="autocomplete-0-label". That label is a <label aria-label="Submit"> wrapping the magnifier submit button (title "Submit"), so the combobox and the input inside it are both named "Submit". This is a real accessibility defect: screen readers announce the search field as "Submit". The question is whether 2.4.6 is the right criterion. What sighted users see is a box with placeholder "Search ..." and a magnifier icon, which describes the field's purpose. Only the computed accessible name is wrong. Many auditors would file that under 4.1.2 or 1.3.1 rather than 2.4.6. Others count the <label> element's text alternative as the label shown to AT users, and fail it under 2.4.6. The criterion mapping is open to reasonable disagreement, so I label it uncertain.

judgments.rationale: "View More" at the bottom of the Pots & Pans mega-menu column, linking to /collections/pots-pans, the same URL as the column-title link "Pots & Pans". A reader could take "does not match" to mean "does not identify", and then the claim names the real failure. Because it depends on that reading, I label it uncertain.
